transcript:
Meeting: Windward Systems x Redwood Inference - Partner onramp discovery
Date/time: 2026-04-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Record ID: ff-2026-04-08-windward-01
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Windward - Head of Platform), Diego Morales (Windward - CTO), Amina Kaur (Windward - Infra Lead), Evan Price (Windward - Procurement)

Summary:
Short intro call to understand Windward's GPU ops plans, compliance needs, and to scope a small pilot for model inference. Primary concerns: data residency, private deployment options (VPC / on-prem), performance targets for low-latency inference at scale, and procurement timeline.

Topics:
- Current infra + cloud providers in use (multi-cloud)
- Latency vs cost tradeoffs and dedicated capacity
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) requirements and KMS integration
- Pilot scope and benchmarks (throughput, p50/p95 latency)
- Security/compliance documents and contract timing

Action items: see metadata list above

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Miles, AE at Redwood. Quick round of intros?
[00:00:15] Laura: Hi, Laura Chen here — Head of Platform at Windward. We're looking into inference options for our customer-facing recommendation engine.
[00:00:22] Diego: Diego Morales, CTO. Big picture is low latency, predictable cost and we need auditability for regulated clients.
[00:00:29] Amina: Amina Kaur, infra. I run the GPU infra and deployments, so the nitty gritty is mine.
[00:00:35] Evan: Evan Price, procurement, I'll help with timelines and contracting.
[00:00:40] Priya: Hey, Priya Nair, I'm the Solutions Eng for Redwood, I'll go deep on performance and private deploys.
[00:00:48] Jordan: Great. Quick context from our side — Redwood provides hosted APIs, dedicated pools, and a private deployment option that can run in a VPC or on-prem if needed. We focus on predictable inference economics and good observability.
[00:01:05] Laura: Sounds good. We're currently on MajorCloud and also have a small on-prem footprint for PII workloads. We want something that can route traffic depending on data sensitivity.
[00:01:20] Diego: The other constraint is p95 under 120ms for most inference calls; for some customer journeys we need p50 < 50ms. Cost targets are tight — we can't just throw GPUs at it.
[00:01:35] Priya: Okay that's helpful. A few clarifying Qs — what's your current model shape, sequence lengths, and average query tokens? Even rough numbers help us size dedicated pools and advise quantization.
[00:01:50] Amina: Mostly transformer-based recommender, 3–4k seq length occasionally for context, mean is about 256 tokens per request. Throughput is bursty, peaks around 350 qps.
[00:02:05] Jordan: Cool. That burstiness is perfect for a mix of reserved capacity plus burst billing. We can suggest autoscale windows and a KV cache to reduce token costs for repeated prefixes.
[00:02:20] Diego: KV cache — we've heard about that but how opaque is the cache with respect to PII? We can't have cached user content escaping the VPC.
[00:02:30] Priya: Good callout. For Private deployments and Dedicated within a customer's VPC we support customer-managed encryption keys via KMS/HSM, and caching is configurable to be in-memory and within the VPC only — nothing hits Redwood public infra when you choose private. There are tradeoffs for cache warmup and cold start latency though.
[00:02:50] Laura: And for hosted API, what's the retention policy and do you have SOC 2 details?
[00:02:57] Priya: Hosted keeps logs for X days by default — we can change retention on enterprise tiers. We'll share SOC 2 and our network diagram; for SSO we support SAML/SCIM and RBAC.
[00:03:12] Evan: Procurement question — what kind of contract lead time do you need and is there a standard reseller MOU?
[00:03:20] Jordan: We have a partner MOU and standard enterprise agreement; for Dedicated it's usually a 30–45 day procurement cycle but can be accelerated. We'll email the MOU and pricing.
[00:03:35] Amina: For private deploy, does Redwood's control plane sit in our VPC or do you run a control plane that talks to our on-prem?
[00:03:43] Priya: For Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed or hosted in a private tenancy — we offer an option where you run a slim control plane in your VPC and the runtime workers are in your network. For air-gapped on-prem we ship an appliance bundle.
[00:04:00] Diego: What's the effort to get model artifacts onboarded? We use custom fine-tuned models and would prefer not to re-train to fit your runtime.
[00:04:10] Priya: We typically do a compatibility sweep — architecture/ops changes like attention kernel selection and some quantization profiles. Most transformer weights work out of the box; we have an onboarding script and a small model conversion step that usually takes a few hours to a day depending on size.
[00:04:28] Jordan: Pricing question — how do you do per-token vs reserved blocks for embeddings and inferencing?
[00:04:35] Priya: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeds). Dedicated is reserved GPU-hours with overage pricing; we can structure hybrid pricing for pilot phases. Optimize tooling will recommend batching and quantization to hit cost targets.
[00:04:50] Laura: What about multi-region failover? Our users are global and we don't want big latencies if a region has a hiccup.
[00:04:58] Priya: Smart routing can route by region and tier; we can set fallback to a compatible lower-cost quantized variant in another region. That gives better reliability with graceful degradation.
[00:05:12] Diego: Any gotchas with Kubernetes or our infra — e.g., driver versions, cudnn, mixed GPU types?
[00:05:20] Priya: The runtime works best with NVIDIA Ampere+ and we maintain a compatibility matrix. For private deployments we provide a deployment guide with driver and kernel recommendations; heterogeneous GPU pools can be supported but we'll recommend standardizing where possible to avoid perf variance.
[00:05:36] Amina: For benchmarking the p95 target, what's the recommended approach? We want to run an apples-to-apples test.
[00:05:42] Priya: We'll propose a pilot: you give a representative request trace and a sample model weight; we'll run an A/B test on your infra (if private) or our dedicated infra, measure p50/p95, throughput, and token cost. We'll also look at KV cache behavior and steady-state batching.
[00:05:57] Jordan: Nuts-and-bolts — propose 2 week pilot with three test windows: small load, medium sustained, and peak burst. Priya will own the performance report.
[00:06:08] Evan: From procurement angle we may need a pilot PO; typical procurement timeline is 2–3 weeks after receiving SOW.
[00:06:18] Jordan: Noted. We'll send a pilot SOW template.
[00:06:22] Laura: Security — do you support customer-provided KMS keys, and can audit logs be exported to our SIEM?
[00:06:29] Priya: Yes and yes. For private or dedicated we can plug into your KMS and ship logs to your SIEM or S3 with the retention you choose.
[00:06:36] Amina: Any concerns on data residency — we need EU-only processing for some clients.
[00:06:41] Priya: We have region pinning and can ensure worker pools stay in EU regions. For on-prem we obviously keep data local. We'll capture residency constraints in the SOW.
[00:06:52] Diego: Competitors we evaluated — MajorCloudAI (fast but opaque pricing), Infera (good tooling), Veridian Labs (tight enterprise support) — how do you compare?
[00:07:03] Jordan: We position as production-first with predictable economics and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private. You'll get transparent latency/cost tradeoffs and first-class observability.
[00:07:14] Priya: Also our Optimize module gives quantization and batching recommendations tied to actual workload, which helps hit the cost targets without big quality regressions.
[00:07:25] Amina: One more ops question — how do upgrades work for private deployments? We want minimal downtime.
[00:07:30] Priya: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks; for private you control the maintenance window and we can provide offline upgrade tooling for air-gapped setups.
[00:07:42] Laura: Ok this is good. Next steps from our side: Amina will prepare a sample trace and a S3 test bucket. Evan will coordinate procurement constraints.
[00:07:53] Jordan: From Redwood: I'll send pricing and SOW template; Priya will share security docs and the deployment guide. We'll aim to have those out by next Monday.
[00:08:05] Diego: Timeline — if pilot runs mid-April we hope to decide on Dedicated by May 1st.
[00:08:12] Jordan: We'll try to hit that. Any final questions?
[00:08:16] Evan: Nothing else. Thanks.
[00:08:18] Laura: Thanks all.
[00:08:20] Priya: Thanks — we'll follow up with links.
[00:08:25] Jordan: Meeting adjourned.
